Dense inline styles

The E2 count case, and the one that decides the design. 2,000 elements are present simultaneously, each carrying a page-authored style attribute. Nothing animates — the pressure is purely how many elements exist at once.

This sits deliberately at the measured crossover. Blink indexes CSS rules by the rightmost compound selector, so per-element structural selectors (which must end in a tag or a page-authored class, because adding an id or class is the mutation the invariant forbids) all land in a single bucket: every candidate element then tests every rule. That is O(M²), measured at ~22ns per element×rule, and it costs that on every full style pass, not once.

At M=2,000 the matching overhead alone was measured at ~89ms against ARCHITECTURE.md §9's 100ms budget — so this fixture is the line between "per-element selector emission works" and "it does not". The rest of the corpus cannot see this: its median is zero inline-styled elements and its previous maximum was 141.
